sbh2.1:1.5: The pervasive object [vyāpī-ālambana], the conduct-purifying object [carita-viśodhana], the skill object [kauśalya], and the defilement-purifying object [kleśa-viśodhana].
sbh2.1:2.4: namely, the image with conceptual construction [savikalpa-pratibimba], the image without conceptual construction [nirvikalpa-pratibimba], the full extent of the substance [vastu-paryantatā],
sbh2.1:2.5: and the consummation of the work [kārya-pariniṣpatti].
sbh2.1:3.1: What is the image with conceptual construction?
sbh2.1:3.2: A certain person, relying on hearing the true dharma or on instruction-and-counsel, taking what has been seen, heard, or imagined, investigates — by aspects of *vipaśyanā* grounded in the concentrated plane — an image-with-conceptual-construction conformable to the substance to be known [jñeya-vastu].
sbh2.1:4.1: What is the substance to be known?
sbh2.1:4.2: Namely: unattractiveness [aśubha], lovingkindness [maitrī], this-conditional dependent origination [idaṃ-pratyayatā pratītya-samutpāda], the analysis of elements [dhātu-prabheda], and mindfulness of breathing [ānāpāna-smṛti];
sbh2.1:4.4: the grossness of the lower planes,
sbh2.1:4.5: the calmness of the upper planes, the truth of arising, the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path. This is called the substance to be known.
sbh2.1:5.1: With respect to this substance-to-be-known: having come to instruction or hearing of the true dharma, and relying on that, he manifests attention grounded in the concentrated plane and resolves on those very dharmas.
sbh2.1:5.2: Thus he resolves on the substance-to-be-known.
sbh2.1:5.3: At that time, the resolve proceeds either as ‘experienced through direct perception’
sbh2.1:5.6: gathered close, manifest; not, however, as a thing of that very kind, but as a resolve-experience.
sbh2.1:5.7: It is such a kind of attention-experience grounded in the concentrated plane by which something corresponding to that substance-to-be-known comes to be —
sbh2.1:5.8: an appearance — and by this it is called
sbh2.1:5.9: an image conformable to the substance-to-be-known.
sbh2.1:5.10: When the practitioner, reviewing this practice, examines that substance-to-be-known under consideration and determines its qualities and faults —
sbh2.1:5.11: this is called the image with conceptual construction.
sbh2.1:6.1: What is the image without conceptual construction?
sbh2.1:6.2: This practitioner, having grasped the sign from the image, no longer investigates,
sbh2.1:6.6: Rather, taking that very object without clinging and by way of the meaning-aspect, he calms that sign.
sbh2.1:6.7: Rather, by the nine-fold mental abiding, he places the mind inwardly,
sbh2.1:6.12: At that time, that image-without-conceptual-construction is his object —
sbh2.1:6.13: where he establishes one-aspected one-pointed mindfulness on the object.
sbh2.1:6.14: That is the object; he does not investigate, deliberate, or thoroughly examine.
sbh2.1:6.15: And that image is simply called an image [pratibimba].
sbh2.1:6.16: These are the alternate names of the image conformable to the substance-to-be-known.
sbh2.1:7.1: What is the substance’s full extent [vastu-paryantatā]?
sbh2.1:7.2: It is the *yāvad-bhāvikatā* (as-far-as-it-goes-ness) of the object, and its *yathāvad-bhāvikatā* (as-it-actually-is-ness).
sbh2.1:7.4: [That] beyond which there is no further form-aggregate, feeling-aggregate, perception-aggregate, formations-aggregate, or consciousness-aggregate —
sbh2.1:7.5: the comprehensive gathering of all conditioned substances by the five [aggregates]; the comprehensive gathering of all dharmas by the elements and bases; the comprehensive gathering of all substances-to-be-known
sbh2.1:7.6: by the noble truths. This is called *yāvad-bhāvikatā*.
sbh2.1:7.9: and its suchness [tathatā], endowed with the reasonings —
sbh2.1:7.11: namely, by dependence-reasoning [apekṣā-yukti], cause-and-effect reasoning [kārya-kāraṇa-yukti], proof-establishing reasoning [upapatti-sādhana-yukti], and nature-of-things reasoning [dharmatā-yukti].
sbh2.1:7.12: Thus the *yāvad-bhāvikatā* and *yathāvad-bhāvikatā* of the object, summarized as one, is called the full extent of the substance.
sbh2.1:8.1: What is the consummation of the work?
sbh2.1:8.2: When, through familiarization, cultivation, and frequent practice, the *śamatha-vipaśyanā* attention with image-as-object
sbh2.1:8.3: is fulfilled — by that fulfillment, the attention with image-as-object [is complete] —
sbh2.1:8.5: By that fulfillment, the support [āśraya] is transformed [parivartate].
sbh2.1:8.7: Through the transformation of the support [āśraya-parivṛtti], transcending the image, there arises in that very substance-to-be-known direct knowing-and-seeing without conceptual construction.
sbh2.1:8.8: This arises for the attainer of the first *dhyāna* in the range of the first *dhyāna*; for the attainer of the second, third, fourth *dhyāna* —
sbh2.1:8.9: for the attainer of the fourth *dhyāna* —
sbh2.1:8.10: in the range of the fourth *dhyāna*; and for the attainer of the *ākāśānantyāyatana*, *vijñānānantyāyatana*, *ākiñcanyāyatana*, and *naivasaṁjñā-nāsaṁjñāyatana* attainments, in their respective ranges.
sbh2.1:8.11: This is called the consummation of the work.
sbh2.1:9.3: Universal, present in all objects, taught by the past, future, and present perfectly-awakened ones.
sbh2.1:9.4: Therefore it is called the [Damaged/Conjectural: pervasive] object.
sbh2.1:9.5: Furthermore, this object [pertains] both to the *śamatha* side and to the *vipaśyanā* side; it has all-substance-ness, true-substance-ness, and cause-effect-substance-ness.
sbh2.1:10.1: [As to] ‘the image with conceptual construction’ — this is on the *vipaśyanā* side.
sbh2.1:10.2: [As to] ‘the full extent of the substance’ — this concerns all-substance-ness and true-substance-ness.
sbh2.1:10.3: [As to] ‘the consummation of the work’ — this is the cause-effect connection.
sbh2.1:11.1: As spoken by the Blessed One, addressing the venerable Revata.
sbh2.1:11.3: The venerable Revata asked the Blessed One a question.
sbh2.1:11.4: "To what extent, venerable sir, is a monk-yogī-yogācāra one whose mind is bound to an object? In which object does he bind the mind?
sbh2.1:11.5: How, further, is the mind well-bound to the object?"
sbh2.1:11.6: "Excellent, Revata, excellent. You ask me well, Revata.
sbh2.1:11.8: Therefore listen, attend well; I will speak.
sbh2.1:11.9: Here, Revata, the monk-yogī-yogācāra, wishing to purify conduct, or to develop skill,
sbh2.1:11.10: or to liberate the mind from outflows —
sbh2.1:11.11: binds the mind to a suitable object.
sbh2.1:11.12: He binds it to a corresponding object, properly.
sbh2.1:11.13: There he is one who does not reject [the contemplation].
sbh2.1:12.1: How does he bind the mind to a suitable object?
sbh2.1:12.2: If, Revata, this monk-yogī-yogācāra is of lust-conduct, he does not bind the mind to an attractive object [śubha-ālambana].
sbh2.1:12.3: Thus he binds it to a suitable object.
sbh2.1:12.4: The hatred-conduct one [binds it] to lovingkindness; the delusion-conduct one to this-conditional dependent origination; the conceit-conduct one to the analysis of elements.
sbh2.1:12.5: If, Revata, this monk-yogī-yogācāra is of applied-thought-conduct, he binds the mind to mindfulness of breathing.
sbh2.1:12.6: Thus he binds it to a suitable object.
sbh2.1:13.1: If, Revata, this monk is confused about the specific characteristic of conditioned things but binds the mind to skill, [it is suitable].
sbh2.1:13.2: The cause-confused [binds it to] skill-in-elements; the condition-confused to skill-in-bases. One wishing to make dispassion toward the desire-realm [binds the mind to] the grossness of sense-pleasures and the calmness of forms; one wishing dispassion toward forms —
sbh2.1:13.3: binds the mind to the grossness of forms and the calmness of the formless.
sbh2.1:13.4: Or, one wishing disenchantment with the *satkāya* and liberation [binds the mind to] the truth of suffering, the truth of arising, the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path.
sbh2.1:13.6: binds the mind to a suitable object.
sbh2.1:14.1: Here, Revata, whatever the monk wishes to investigate as the substance-to-be-known — wishes to investigate closely,
sbh2.1:14.4: that has been previously seen by him,
sbh2.1:14.6: Taking that very seen-heard-thought-cognized as governing, with attention grounded in the concentrated plane, he attends to it.
sbh2.1:14.8: He does not see that very substance-to-be-known itself made present in concentration; rather, a representation of it arises.
sbh2.1:14.9: Its appearance, a mere knowing, a mere seeing, a mere remembered-mark — that is the object. This monk-yogī-yogācāra binds the mind properly to the object.
sbh2.1:15.1: If, Revata, this monk-yogī-yogācāra binds the mind to the object to the full extent that the knowable substance is to be known —
sbh2.1:15.2: and [knows] it as it actually is, with an unperverted mind — thus indeed, Revata, this monk-yogī-yogācāra
sbh2.1:15.3: binds the mind properly to the object.
sbh2.1:15.4: And how, Revata, is this monk-yogī-yogācāra non-rejecting in his contemplation?
sbh2.1:15.5: If, Revata, this monk is thus properly applied in the object, of continuous-application,
sbh2.1:15.7: from time to time he cultivates the sign of *śamatha*,
sbh2.1:15.8: the sign of taking-up [effort], and the sign of equanimity. Through familiarization, cultivation, and frequent practice, all encumbrances are tranquillized, and he attains purity-of-support.
sbh2.1:15.11: By examining the substance-to-be-known, [he attains] purity-of-object; by dispassion-from-lust, purity-of-mind; by dispassion-from-ignorance —
sbh2.1:15.12: he attains purity-of-knowing. He touches, contacts, realizes.
sbh2.1:16.2: "The yogī who moves in signs, knowing all the meaning of true substance —
sbh2.1:17.1: When he says 'moving in signs' — by this the *śamatha*-sign, the taking-up-sign, the equanimity-sign, and the constancy of action in them, are named.
sbh2.1:17.2: When he says 'knowing all the meaning of true substance' — by this, *vastu-paryantatā* (the substance's full extent) is named.
sbh2.1:17.3: When he says 'the image-contemplator, sustained' — by this, the image-with-conceptual-construction and the image-without-conceptual-construction are named.
sbh2.1:17.4: When he says 'attains purity' — by this, the consummation of the work is named.
sbh2.1:18.1: Again it has been said by the Blessed One:
sbh2.1:18.2: “The one skilled in the sign of mind knows the taste of seclusion and the seclusion-state —
sbh2.1:18.3: the contemplator, prudent, mindful, eats the rapture-and-happiness free of worldly attachments [nir-āmiṣa].”
sbh2.1:19.1: When he says ‘skilled in the sign of mind’ — by this, the image with conceptual construction and the image without conceptual construction [savikalpa- and nirvikalpa-pratibimba] are named under the term ‘sign.’
sbh2.1:19.3: When he says ‘knows the taste of seclusion and seclusion-state’ — by this, the delight-in-abandonment and delight-in-cultivation of the one properly applied to the object are named.
sbh2.1:19.4: When he says ‘contemplator, careful, mindful’ — by this, the constancy of *śamatha-vipaśyanā* cultivation is named.
sbh2.1:19.5: When he says ‘eats rapture-and-happiness free of worldly attachments’ — by this, the consummation of the work is named.
sbh2.1:19.6: Thus indeed this *vyāpī-ālambana* should be known as purified by trustworthy testimony,
sbh2.1:19.8: This is called the pervasive object.
